Surah al-Hadid (Makki or Madani; its verses number twenty-nine)

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah﴾, i.e., every thing declares Him far above any imperfection. The lam (preposition) is extra (mazīdah), and "mā" (what) is used rather than "man" (who) by way of giving precedence to the majority (taghlīban li'l-akthar). ﴿And He is the Mighty (al-ʿAzīz) in His dominion, the Wise (al-Ḥakīm) in His creating.﴾
﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life﴾ by bringing into being, ﴿and causes death﴾ after it.

He is the First (qabla kulli shay' bila bidaya) before everything, without beginning; and the Last (ba'da kulli shay' bila nihaya) after everything, without end; and the Manifest (bil-adilla 'alayhi) by the proofs of Him; and the Hidden ('an idrak al-hawass) from the perception of the senses.

He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days (ayyam), of the days of this world, the first of which is Sunday and the last of which is Friday. Then He istawa (rose/established Himself) over the Throne (al-'arsh), meaning the Kursi (Footstool), in a manner befitting Him. He knows what enters into the earth, such as rain and the dead, and what comes out of it, such as plants and minerals, and what descends from the sky, such as mercy and punishment, and what ascends into it (ya'ruj, meaning yasʿad, rises), such as good and bad deeds. And He is with you (ma'akum) by His knowledge.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn commentary on Surah 57, verse 5:

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ (The commentary explains:) "all existing things" — جَمِيعها (jamee'uha), i.e., everything that exists.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 6:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾, i.e., makes it enter it, so the night increases and decreases [in length]. ﴿And He causes the day to enter into the night﴾, so the day increases and decreases [in length]. ﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, i.e., of what is in them of secrets and beliefs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 7:

﴿Believe﴾ persist in faith ﴿in God and His Messenger, and spend﴾ in the way of God ﴿of that in which He has made you successors﴾ of the wealth of those who came before you, and those after you will succeed you in it. It was revealed concerning the expedition of hardship (ghazwat al-'usra), which was the expedition of Tabuk. ﴿Those of you who believe and spend﴾ is a reference to 'Uthman, may God be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 8:

﴿And what is wrong with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has taken your covenant (if you are truly believers)?﴾ This is an address to the disbelievers, meaning: there is no obstacle preventing you from faith ﴿in Allah and the Messenger, who calls you to believe in your Lord, and your covenant has been taken﴾ — the verb is read with a damma on the hamza and a kasra on the kha', and also with a fatha on the kha' with the following noun in the accusative, ﴿your covenant﴾ — ﴿upon it﴾, meaning Allah took it in the realm of the atoms (alam al-dharr) when He made them testify against themselves ﴿if you are believers﴾, meaning: if you desire to believe in Him, then hasten to it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 9:

﴿It is He who sends down to His servant clear verses﴾ (the verses of the Qur'an) ﴿that He may bring you out from darkness﴾ (disbelief, kufr) ﴿into light﴾ (faith, iman). ﴿And indeed, Allah is to you﴾ (i.e., in bringing you out from disbelief to faith) ﴿...﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 10:

﴿And what is [wrong] with you﴾, i.e., what is your condition after your faith, ﴿that you do not spend in the way of Allah﴾. Here the nūn of an-na (that) is assimilated into the lām of lā (not), ﴿and to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾, with what is in them; so your wealth will return to Him without any reward for spending, unlike if you had spent, whereupon you would be rewarded. ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ of Mecca ﴿and fought. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought.﴾ And each [of the two groups] ﴿Allah has promised the best﴾, i.e., Paradise. (In one reading, "kullan" is in the nominative, as the subject of the sentence.) ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, so He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 11:

﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah⁠﴾ by spending his wealth in the way of Allah, ﴿a goodly loan⁠﴾ by spending it for the sake of Allah, ﴿and He will multiply it⁠﴾ — and in another reading, "fa-yuda'ʿifahu" (with the doubling of the ʿayn, meaning the same), ﴿for him⁠﴾ from ten up to more than seven hundred, as mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah. ﴿And for him⁠﴾, in addition to the multiplication, ﴿is a noble reward⁠﴾ accompanied by divine good pleasure and acceptance.

Remember ﴿the Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands﴾ (i.e., in front of them), and it is said to them: ﴿Good news for you today: gardens﴾ (i.e., enter them).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 13:

﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed: "Look upon us [unzurūna]"﴾ meaning, "Look at us" (abṣirūnā). In another reading, with a fatḥah on the hamzah and a kasrah on the ẓā', it is read as "Give us respite" (amhilūnā). ﴿"That we may take a light [naqtabis]"﴾ meaning, we may take a burning brand (al-qabas) and illumination ﴿"from your light."﴾ It is said: ﴿"It will be said"﴾ to them, mockingly directed at them: ﴿"Turn back behind you and seek a light."﴾ So they turned back. ﴿"Then a wall will be set up between them"﴾ and the believers ﴿"with a gate. Its inner side will have mercy in it"﴾ on the side of the believers, ﴿"and its outer side"﴾ on the side of the hypocrites. It is said that it is the wall of al-A'raf.

They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?" [In obedience.] They will say, "Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation [by hypocrisy], and you waited [for misfortune to befall the believers], and you doubted [the religion of Islam], and false hopes [desires] deceived you until the command of Allah came [death]. And the Deceiver [Satan] deceived you about Allah."

﴿So today no ransom will be taken﴾ with the ya' and the ta' (بِالياءِ والتّاء), i.e. read as يُؤْخَذ and as تُؤْخَذ, ﴿from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your master﴾ more fitting for you (أوْلى بِكُم), ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾ it (هِيَ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 16:

﴿Has the time not come﴾ (yahin: has come near) ﴿for those who believe﴾. It was revealed concerning the Companions when they engaged in much joking. ﴿that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and what has been revealed﴾ (read with tashdid and with takhfif) ﴿of the truth﴾, the Qur'an. ﴿And that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term grew long for them﴾ (wa lā yakūnū is coordinated with takhsha') ﴿those who were given the Scripture before﴾ are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿The term grew long for them﴾: the time between them and their prophets. ﴿So their hearts became hard﴾, not softened to the remembrance of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 17:

﴿Know﴾ is an address to the believers mentioned (before), ﴿that Allah gives life to the earth after its death﴾ with vegetation, so likewise He does to your hearts, returning them to humility; ﴿We have certainly made the signs clear to you﴾ which indicate Our power through this and other than this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, those who give charity (al-muṣṣaddiqīn)﴾: it comes from taṣaddaqa (to give charity), and the tā' has been assimilated into the ṣād, meaning those who gave charity. ﴿And those who give charity (al-muṣṣaddiqāt)﴾: meaning the women who gave charity. In another reading, the ṣād is lightened in both words, deriving from taṣdīq (affirming the truth) and faith (īmān). ﴿And lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾: this refers to males and females together, by way of giving precedence to the masculine. The verb is coordinated with the noun in the relative clause of al-, because in that position it occupies the place of a verb. Mentioning the loan with its description after "charity" is a specification of it. ﴿It will be multiplied﴾: in another reading, yuḍa"‘if (with the shadda), meaning their loan.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 19:

﴿And those who believed in Allah and His messengers—those are the ṣiddīqūn (the ones who are most emphatic in affirmation), and the shuhadā' (the martyrs/witnesses) with their Lord, (witnessing) against the deniers among the nations. For them is their reward and their light. But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs (the ones indicating Our oneness)—those are the companions of the Jaḥīm (the Fire).﴾

Note: the first two sentences are concise renderings; the gloss "(the Fire)" follows al-Jalāl's gloss on al-Jaḥīm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 20:

﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and diversion and adornment﴾ (tazyin: decoration, making attractive) ﴿and boasting among yourselves and competition in wealth and children﴾; i.e., preoccupation with them. As for acts of obedience and what helps toward them, these are among the matters of the Hereafter. ﴿Like the example of﴾; i.e., it is in its allurement for you and its passing away like the example of ﴿rain﴾ (ghayth: rain, downpour) ﴿whose vegetation pleased the disbelievers﴾ (al-kuffar: the farmers) ﴿—its growth that arises from it. Then it dries up﴾ (yahij: it becomes dry, withers) ﴿and you see it turned yellow. Then it becomes debris﴾ (hutam: crumbled fragments) which is scattered by the winds. ﴿And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment﴾ for those who preferred the world over it, ﴿and forgiveness from Allah and approval﴾ for those who did not prefer the world over it. ﴿And what is the life of this world?﴾; i.e., what is enjoyment in it.

﴿Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth﴾ — [i.e., if] one of them were joined to the other. Al-ʿArḍ (the width) means the expanse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 22:

﴿No calamity befalls on the earth﴾ such as drought, ﴿nor in yourselves﴾ such as sickness and the loss of a child, ﴿except that it is in a Book﴾ meaning the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), ﴿before We bring it into being﴾ i.e., before We create it. It is also said that the same applies to blessings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 23:

﴿So that﴾ "kay" (lam al-kay, the particle that governs the verb in the subjunctive) here has the meaning of "an" (that); i.e., God has informed of this ﴿so that you do not despair﴾ grieve ﴿over what has escaped you, nor exult﴾ in arrogant exultation, but rather with the exultation of gratitude for the blessing ﴿in what He has given you﴾ — with the long vowel ("ātākum") meaning "gave you," and with the short vowel ("ājākum") meaning "came to you from Him" ﴿God does not love any arrogant﴾ boastful ﴿one who boasts﴾ of what he has been given ﴿and is proud﴾ of it ﴿over people﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on Surah 57, verse 24:

﴿Those who are miserly﴾ with what is obligatory upon them, ﴿and enjoin upon people miserliness﴾ with it for themselves. For them there is a severe threat. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ from what is obligatory upon him, ﴿then indeed Allah, He is﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl, a pronoun placed between subject and predicate to separate them and mark the predicate), and in another reading it is recited without it, ﴿the Self-Sufficient﴾ above any other, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ to His allies.

We sent Our messengers, meaning the angels, to the prophets ﴿with clear proofs﴾, meaning decisive arguments, ﴿and sent down with them the Book﴾, meaning the books, ﴿and the Balance﴾, meaning justice, ﴿so that people may uphold justice﴾. ﴿And We sent down iron﴾, meaning We brought it out of the ores, ﴿in which is great might﴾, with which one fights, ﴿and benefits for people﴾. ﴿And so that Allah may know﴾ with ʿilm mushāhada (knowledge by direct observation), coordinated with "so that people may uphold justice", ﴿who helps Him﴾, meaning helps His religion with weapons of war made of iron and other things, ﴿and His messengers unseen﴾. This is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) relating to the hāʾ (ه) in yanṣuruhu, meaning unseen by them in the world. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "They help Him but do not see Him." ﴿Indeed Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾: He has no need of help, but it benefits the one who gives it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 26:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Book.﴾ It means the four books: the Tawrah (Torah), the Injil (Gospel), the Zabur (Psalms) and the Furqan (Criterion, i.e. the Qur'an), for they are in the offspring of Abraham.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 57, verse 27:

﴿Then We sent, following in their footsteps, Our messengers, and We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, and monasticism﴾, which is the abandonment of women and the taking of monasteries (ṣawāmiʿ), ﴿they invented it﴾ on their own accord, ﴿We did not prescribe it for them﴾, We did not command them to it, ﴿except﴾ but they did it ﴿seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, seeking His good pleasure, ﴿but they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾, since many of them abandoned it, disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, and entered the religion of their king. Many of them remained upon the religion of Jesus, so they believed in our Prophet, ﴿and We gave those who believed﴾ in him [their reward].

O you who have believed (in Jesus), fear Allah and believe in His Messenger (Muhammad (ﷺ) and Jesus), and He will give you a double portion of His mercy (ﷺ — namely two shares, kifl̈ayn, for your belief in the prophets), and will make for you a light by which you walk (over the Sirat, the bridge over Hell).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 57, Verse 29:**

﴿So that the People of the Book may know﴾, i.e., "I informed you of that so that they may know." **Ahl al-Kitab** (People of the Book) refers to the **Tawrah** (Torah), those who did not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ). **An** is the light form (**mukhaffafah**) of the heavy **an** (**al-thaqilah**), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (**damir al-sha'n**). The meaning is that they **﴿have no power over anything of Allah's bounty﴾**, contrary to their claim that they are the beloved of Allah and the people of His good pleasure. **﴿And that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whomever He wills﴾**, i.e., He gives it, **﴿whom He wills﴾**. So He gave the believers among them their reward twice, as has been mentioned earlier.
